existing_dashboard_modification: The record counter, the gauge numbers, the gauge arcs and the CSV export were all derived from a summary computed in two places. The spine's apply() drove the counter and the gauges; the wider-fleet cartridge recomputed the same quantities and wrote only the gauge text. Everything it did not write kept the previous technology's answer on all twenty wider-fleet technologies -- the counter's four figures and its dataset, and the three gauge arcs, which are painted by updateChart and were byte-identical on toDataURL across a switch. EXPORT FILTERED CSV was worse: it mapped the spine's `filtered` array, which holds indices into the spine's own payload, so one flywheel on screen exported 3,563 solar rows and reported that count as fact. This release replaces the duplicated calculation with presentSummary(), which the spine's apply() and the cartridge's renderWider() both call, and which owns all four surfaces. A cut that is not the spine's own supplies an export provider; the wider fleet's declines, naming the ten of the CSV's fifty columns it could fill and what the other forty are. No spine behaviour changes: apply() passes no provider, so the product's own export path is the one it always was.
